title: Is the historic Hannah House haunted? When you can check it out for yourself
excerpt: The Historic Hannah House has long been known as a 'haunted' location. See what volunteers told us about the ghostly vibes.
content:
Sept. 25, 2026, 5:04 a.m. ET

When you step through the door of this historic Italianate home on the south side, the decor and architecture takes you to another time.

Some believe its history is still alive — it's become a destination for paranormal enthusiasts, though volunteers say it has a vibe that's more friendly than spooky.

The home was built in 1858, three years before the Civil War began, and used to sit on 400 acres of farmland.

The Historic Hannah House has long been known as a significant property when it comes to Indianapolis history and local hauntings. The home has long been considered to be one of the most haunted houses in the state.

While it has become a place many paranormal investigators travel to stay overnight, it is more than that. It is also a beautiful home where couples have gotten married, where history buffs can take tours to learn about the home and local history. It's a place where people in the community come together and help out however they can to keep a property with a rich history going. The home is completely run by volunteers.

Hannah House is currently under renovation, with much of the work being done by the owner himself, Paul Gartin, a self-described "jack-of-all-trades."

His great grandparents, the Oehler's, bought the home after the Hannah family, for which the house is named, died. Roman Oehler was a watchmaker and owned a jewelry shop that was located at 183 W. Washington Street. Gartin's grandmother grew up in the home, as well as his great uncles. Gartin himself lived in the home for a short while. The home was later passed down to him.

"I came back four years ago because the place was kind of falling down and I got reinvolved, and so now I got the full extent of having the fun of keeping it going," Gartin said. "I'd like to keep it open for down the road."

Gartin hopes the home can become more a part of the community and hopes hosting more events, like the Haunted House and their first ever Trunk or Treat, will show that Hannah House is a place for everyone, whether you like history, architecture or spirits.

The property was closed or only partially open for several years, but now is working toward being a place for the public again.

"There's still people to this day who have never been here," Gartin said. "They don't know we're back and hopefully we're going to be around a lot longer."

Hannah House is considered one of the most haunted homes in Indy

It's local lore that Hannah House used to be a stop on the Underground Railroad, and historians have confirmed that the house's original owner, Alexander Hannah, was an abolitionist.

As the legend goes, one night, a group of slaves died when an overturned gas lamp caused a fire where they slept. It is believed Hannah secretly buried their bodies in his basement for fear of being penalized for his role in the Underground Railroad.

Despite the numerous reports of ghost activity, those who volunteer and spend a lot of time on the property say it is a warm and welcoming place.

"Everything here is positive," Theresa Curtis said. "It's comforting like home. They want to interact with you. They want to be known."

Curtis has been volunteering at Hannah House for three years and is credited as the resident history expert. Curtis grew up in Indy and her grandmother lived near the property. She fondly remembers always being fascinated by the home.

"Every time we drove by here I would always go 'Oh I love that house,'" Curtis said.

Tim and Marisa Pullan are fascinated by the paranormal and first arrived at the house for their annual Paranormal Festival that takes place on the property in August. Tim is a bit skeptical and tries to debunk things. But his wife Marisa, says she can feel when a spirit is in the room and sometimes hears or sees things others do not. They shared why the home is so popular among ghost hunters.

"A lot of people that have come here have witnessed things, have gotten good data and quite frankly, it's an old house. It's seen a lot," Tim Pullan said. "There's plenty of other places here in Indy where you can go and do paranormal investigations, but very few have the kind of history and activity that this place has."

The owner believes there is nothing bad in the home and he doesn't want anything bad to be brought in, so Ouija boards are forbidden.

Hannah House hosts first Trunk or Treat for community outreach

At the Paranormal Festival in August, the Pullans were captivated by the home and asked how they could get involved. This year, they are running the Haunted House experience.

Hannah House is starting off spooky season by hosting their first ever Trunk or Treat event on Thursday, Oct. 1 from 6-8 p.m. as a free event to welcome the community to the property.

To learn more about the event or sign up to participate to pass out candy, visit the official Historic Hannah House Facebook page or visit the event page.

Hannah's Nightmares, the 2026 haunted house experience

The Haunted House experience will happen every Friday and Saturday from 7-11 p.m. starting Oct. 2 through Oct. 31. This experience is also completely run by volunteers so the actors and everyone involved are all people who are donating their time to help put this on for the community.

If your little one might be too scared, they're offering two "lights-on" experiences, which will be from 4-6 p.m. Oct. 9 and Oct. 23.

Tickets for the Haunted House are $25 per person and available for purchase on-site at the ticket booth.

"We're here for [Paul], and we're here for the house, and we try to support where we can," Tim said. "When we bring money in, 100% of it goes back to the house. Like he doesn't make a living off of this, he does it because he loves the place. It's his family's home."

To learn more about the Haunted House experience, visit historichannahhouse.net or the Facebook page for the event, Hannah's Nightmares.

Historic tours happening monthly at Hannah House

If you're more intrigued by the history of the home, the property has an Open House Historic Tour from 1-4 p.m. on the first Sunday of every month. Tickets are $10 per person, but children 12 and younger are free.

All the proceeds go directly back into the care, maintenance and restoration of the home.

If you're interested in checking it out during the spookiest time of year, the next open house will take place on Sunday, Oct. 4.

Visit historichannahhouse.net to learn more about renting the venue for a wedding, special event or request a private tour.
